method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, definition-by-definition model-theoretic replay, forward and reverse proof reconstruction for validity, unsatisfiability, monotonicity and semantic deduction, verification of the quantified closed-term consequences, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Validity, logical truth, semantic entailment, satisfiability and unsatisfiability, monotonicity, the semantic deduction theorem, and quantified consequences for closed terms.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A sentence is valid, or a logical truth, when every structure satisfies it regardless of the interpretation of nonlogical symbols. Gamma entails A when every structure satisfying Gamma satisfies A. Gamma is satisfiable when some structure satisfies it, and otherwise unsatisfiable.
samples.checks: Every/some quantifier force, logical/nonlogical distinction, syntactic-structure qualification and all three displayed notations are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A is valid exactly when every sentence set Gamma entails A. Validity gives the forward direction immediately; if A is invalid, a counterstructure also satisfies the valid singleton {truth}, producing a Gamma that does not entail A.
samples.checks: The universal range over premise sets, counterpositive direction, singleton choice, validity of truth and countermodel are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma entails A exactly when Gamma together with not-A is unsatisfiable. A satisfying structure for the union would satisfy both A and not-A; conversely, unsatisfiability says every structure either fails Gamma or satisfies A.
samples.checks: Both directions, union membership consequences, contradiction and final entailment condition are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercises connect contradiction with unsatisfiability and quantify over a fresh constant. Entailment is monotone: any model of a larger premise set Gamma-prime is a model of its subset Gamma and therefore satisfies every consequence of Gamma.
samples.checks: All three exercise biconditionals, freshness scope, subset direction and model-inclusion reasoning are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The semantic deduction theorem moves A between the premise set and the antecedent of a conditional. Both proof directions fix an arbitrary structure satisfying the relevant premise set and use the material-conditional satisfaction clause.
samples.checks: The displayed biconditional, assumption-set unions, conditional antecedent/consequent, satisfaction transfers and both entailment conclusions are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For A(x) with only x free and a closed term t, A(t) entails the existential closure and the universal closure entails A(t). An assignment mapping x to the value of t connects the quantified satisfaction theorem with semantic substitution and sentence satisfaction.
samples.checks: Closedness, both tagged entailments, assignment value, sentence status, three cited propositions and the proof-completion prompt are retained.

source_observations: No deterministic frozen-source defect requiring a Marathi correction was found in this unit.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match the frozen source exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact Marathi entailment, satisfiability, unsatisfiability, semantic-deduction and logical-truth terms remain explicitly open to specialist review in T123, T124, T148, T150 and T224.
